queries_attempted: user feedback collection and prioritization software
customer feedback platform for product managers

competitors.name: Productboard
competitors.notes: Purpose-built for product feedback and prioritization. Collects from multiple channels (email, Intercom, Zendesk, etc.), prioritization using impact/effort scoring. Full feature overlap.
competitors.feature_overlap: Feedback collection from multiple sources, prioritization, roadmap integration, analysis
competitors.market_positioning: Product management platform for customer-driven roadmaps

competitors.name: Canny
competitors.notes: Collect feedback via widget, API, email, integrations. Prioritization with voting and tags. Full feature overlap.
competitors.feature_overlap: Feedback collection, voting, prioritization, roadmap, changelog
competitors.market_positioning: Simple feedback management for SaaS teams

competitors.name: Aha!
competitors.notes: Product roadmap and feedback management. Collect from multiple sources, prioritize with scoring. Full feature overlap.
competitors.feature_overlap: Feedback collection, prioritization, roadmap, strategy alignment
competitors.market_positioning: Product roadmap software with feedback management

competitors.name: UserVoice
competitors.notes: Feedback collection, prioritization, roadmap. Integrations with support tools. Full feature overlap.
competitors.feature_overlap: Feedback collection, voting, prioritization, roadmap, support integration
competitors.market_positioning: Customer feedback platform for product teams

competitors.name: Frill
competitors.notes: Feedback collection widget, roadmap, changelog. Integrations. Full feature overlap.

competitors.name: Featurebase
competitors.notes: Feedback board, roadmap, changelog. Integrations. Full feature overlap.
competitors.market_positioning: Feedback and roadmap for product teams

competitors.name: Nolt
competitors.notes: Feedback board, voting, roadmap. Full feature overlap.

competitors.name: Upvoty
competitors.notes: Feedback board, roadmap, changelog. Full feature overlap.

competitors.name: Fider
competitors.notes: Open source feedback board. Self-hosted. Partial feature overlap – lacks automatic multi-channel collection but can be extended via API.

competitors.name: FeatureHub
competitors.notes: Open source feature management and feedback. Partial overlap – more focused on feature flags but includes feedback.

competitors.name: Intercom (Product Tours, Inbox)
competitors.notes: Intercom offers feedback collection via surveys, inbox, and product tours. Not purpose-built for prioritization but can serve as a substitute.

competitors.name: Zendesk (Support + Gather)
competitors.notes: Zendesk Gather is a feedback community. Support tickets also capture feedback. Partial overlap – lacks dedicated prioritization features.

competitors.name: HubSpot Service Hub
competitors.notes: Feedback surveys, ticketing, and customer service. Partial overlap – not a dedicated feedback prioritization tool.

competitors.name: Trello / Asana / Notion
competitors.notes: General project management tools that can be manually configured to collect and prioritize feedback. Low feature overlap – no automatic collection or analysis.

competitors.name: Spreadsheets (Excel / Google Sheets)
competitors.notes: Common workaround – manually export and categorize feedback. No automation or analysis.

summary: The market for product feedback management and prioritization is crowded with multiple well-established direct competitors (Productboard, Canny, Aha!, UserVoice, Frill, Featurebase, Nolt, Upvoty) that cover the full JTBD: automatic collection from multiple channels, organization, analysis, and prioritization. Additionally, platform-native features (Intercom, Zendesk, HubSpot) and open-source alternatives (Fider, FeatureHub) provide partial or substitute solutions. The current workaround (spreadsheets) is a weak substitute but widely used. The competitive landscape scores 4 (crowded market) because there are many credible purpose-built alternatives with strong feature overlap and competitive pricing. A new entrant would need significant differentiation (e.g., AI-driven analysis, unique integrations, or a specific niche) to gain traction.
